title: Terraform primer + capacity scout for private install prechecks
creator: Tomas Gil
description:
Summary: Build a robust, reproducible preflight toolchain ("preflight-scout") that runs Terraform/IaC-aware validation and live environment probes before Private (VPC) installs. Scope includes quota discovery (core, regional, GPU SKUs), Terraform service principal IAM verification, DNS/private-zone resolution checks, networking primitives (subnets/CIDR/reachability), and GPU capacity/availability heuristics.

Goals:
- Provide a single CLI and CI job that validates customer-target accounts/regions prior to provisioning Redwood Private.
- Surface actionable, remediable failures (quota requests, IAM grants, DNS zone ownership, NACL/route blockers, no-GPU-capacity) with guidance links and Terraform snippets to fix.
- Integrate Terraform plan parsing to detect missing required resources or incompatible module versions before apply.
- Emit machine-readable results (JSON) to S3/Artifacts and a human-friendly summary for Solutions/SEs.

Checks to implement:
1) Quotas: query cloud provider quota APIs (compute cores, GPUs per SKU, elastic IPs, IPv4 addresses, NAT gateway limits) and compare against expected minima for requested cluster sizes. Include historical quota usage sampling where available.
2) GPU capacity probe: if quota exists, probe available SKU capacity in region/zone using soft-capacity endpoint(s) or partner APIs; when not available, fallback to heuristics: recent allocation trends + partner capacity signals.
3) IAM & TF service principal: validate Terraform service account has policies for creating/attaching roles, creating KMS keys, managing IAM roles, and registering VPC endpoints. Use both simulated policy evaluation and an actual dry-run creation of a harmless resource (tagged) to detect implicit denies.
4) DNS: ensure private DNS zone exists or that delegation records can be created; test resolution from a temporary probe instance in the target VPC (or run egress DNS test for managed zones). Validate forwarders and conditional forwarders where enterprise networks require them.
5) Networking: verify CIDR non-overlap with existing customer networks, route-table propagation, IGW/NAT presence for egress dependencies, and subnet tagging conventions required by our Terraform modules.
6) Terraform module compatibility: parse module versions, deprecated inputs, and provider versions from root module and terraform lock file. Fail with suggested module pins or upgrades when incompatible.
7) KMS/HSM & encryption: validate KMS key policies and grant ability for Redwood runtime principal to encrypt/decrypt and generate data keys.
8) Observability & Rollback hooks: ensure that monitoring roles/agents can be installed, log retention buckets accessible, and that automatic rollback hooks can be attached to apply workflows.

Deliverables:
- preflight-scout CLI (Go) with two modes: static (Terraform plan parsing) and live (API probes).
- A reusable Terraform module that can be invoked in a tenant account to create lightweight probe resources and then destroy them.
- CI job templates and GitHub Actions for use by SE and onboarding flow.
- Console dashboard card (link stub) that surfaces recent preflight runs & failure rates.
- Playbook for Solutions Engineers with remediation snippets for the top 10 most common failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preflight-scout returns a deterministic JSON report with top-level pass/fail and per-check details and remediation steps.
- False positive rate for capacity checks under 10% in a small pilot of 25 customer regions.
- Terraform plan parser detects >=90% of incompatible module inputs in our test corpus.
- SE playbook validated by 2 SEs in the onboarding team and one postmortem from a pilot install.

Implementation notes & tradeoffs:
- We will prefer cloud provider quota APIs where possible; where provider APIs are insufficient for capacity prediction for GPUs we will implement a probabilistic heuristic and surface confidence scores.
- Simulated IAM evaluation is faster but can miss SCP/organization-level denies; a lightweight, tagged probe create may be necessary for high-confidence checks.
- DNS probing may be restricted in air-gapped customers; fallbacks include requiring the customer to run a local probe container and upload results.
- For multi-tenant Dedicated pools, capacity signals will be conservative to avoid over-promising.

Links & artifacts:
- Terraform module prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probes/terraform-preflight (prototype PR linked in comments)
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Preflight+Scout+Design
- Pilot dashboard (internal): https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/preflight-scout
